s: rhododendron (flowering shrub in the genus Rhododendron)
Rhine (a major river in Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany, France and the Netherlands, emptying into the North Sea)
Sie sollen ihn nicht haben, / Den freien deutschen Rhein, / Bis seine Fluth begraben / Des letzten Mann’s Gebein.
They shall not have him, / The free German Rhine, / Until his flood has covered / The last man's bones.
Rhein.et: From Middle High German Rīn, from Old High German Rīn, from Proto-West Germanic *Rīn (“the river Rhine”). The spelling with Rh- after Latin Rhenus, itself possibly a Hellenizing form.

s: Rhone, Rhône (a major river in Switzerland and France that flows from the Alps to the Mediterranean Sea)
Rhone.et: Borrowed from Middle French Rho(s)ne. 16th century or earlier. Partially displaced older Rotten, which see. All ultimately from Latin Rhodanus.

s: rhubarb (any plant of the genus Rheum, especially Rheum rhabarbarum, having large leaves and long green or reddish acidic leafstalks that are edible, in particular when cooked (although the leaves are mildly poisonous))

rhubarb (the leafstalks of common rhubarb or garden rhubarb (usually known as Rheum × hybridum), which are long, fleshy, often pale red, and with a tart taste, used as a food ingredient; they are frequently stewed with sugar and made into jam or used in crumbles, pies, etc)
Rhabarber.et: From Italian rabarbaro, from Latin rhabarbarum, reubarbarum, from Ancient Greek ῥῆον βαρβαρικόν (rhêon barbarikón).

s: rhythm (variation of strong and weak emphasis over time, e.g. in music or speech)
pattern, rhythm (series of repetitive events or actions spaced out evenly)
rhesus monkey, rhesus macaque, Macaca mulatta
Rhesusaffe.et: From French rhésus + Affe (“ape, monkey”), partial calque of French singe rhésus.

Rhetorik.et:
From Middle High German rhetorica/retorica, from Latin rhētorica, from Ancient Greek ῥητορικός (rhētorikós).
Compare French rhétorique.

s: Rhineland (geographical region in western Germany, roughly equivalent to the former Prussian Rhine Province)
Ein Rhomboeder ist ein Polyeder, das von 6 Rauten begrenzt ist.
rheology (physics of the deformation and flow of matter)
Im Saal brandet Applaus auf, er geht schnell über in rhythmisches Klatschen.
Applause surges in the hall, it quickly changes into rhythmic clapping.
metropolis on the Rhine: Cologne (Köln) or Düsseldorf

Rheumatismus.et: Early 18th century, from Latin rheumatismus, from Ancient Greek ῥευματισμός (rheumatismós).

s: Er liegt nicht so bequem in Bezug auf die Einfahrt zur Stadt, aber eben so bequem für den Anschluß an den Rhein und die Weiterführung der Bahn rheinaufwärts.
It is not as conveniently located for entry to the town, but it is just as convenient for connections to the Rhine and the continuation of the line upstream.
Immer wieder schaute er auf "seine" Buran, die auf dem Ponton rheinaufwärts glitt.
He kept looking at "his" Buran, which floated up the Rhine on the pontoon.
Wenn ein Händler beispielsweise genügend Ware eingekauft hatte, so charterte er ein Schiff und führte sie rheinabwärts nach Köln.
When a trader had bought enough goods, for example, he chartered a ship and sailed down the Rhine to Cologne.
Mit rheinabwärts fliessendem, kontaminiertem Wasser steigt die Zahl deutscher Stadtbehörden, die genaue Informationen über die Giftstoffe zu erhalten suchen.
With the contaminated water flowing down the Rhine, the number of German citizens looking for exact information about the toxic chemicals increases.

Rhinozeros.et: From Middle High German rinōceros, from Latin rhīnocerōs, from Ancient Greek ῥῑνόκερως (rhīnókerōs, literally “nose-horned”). The inflected forms in -rosses, -rösser are by association with unrelated Ross (“horse”); the same might also apply to the neuter gend…

s: rhexigenous (of intercellular space, made by tearing apart of cells)
a town in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, now part of the community of Rheda-Wiedenbrück
a town in West Prussia, Germany, now Polish Reda
Das Rheinfränk. wird [...] in das Hessische im NO und das Pfälzisch-Lothringische im SW untergliedert.
Rhine Franconian … is divided into Hessian in the North-East and Palatine-Lothringian in the South-West.
Die fest/feschd - Linie teilt das Rheinfränkische in die Mundarten Hessisch und Pfälzisch-Lothringisch.
The fest/feschd-line divides Rhine Franconian into the dialects Hessian and Palatine-Lothringian.

Rheuma.et: Early 18th century, from Latin rheuma, from Ancient Greek ῥεῦμα (rheûma).

s: rhomboid (A parallelogram which is neither a rhombus nor a rectangle)
Rhomboid.et:
From Latin rhomboīdēs, from Ancient Greek ῥομβοειδής (rhomboeidḗs, “rhombus-shaped”, “rhomboidal”).
Equivalent to Rhombus + -oid.

s: rhomboid (one of certain muscles at the fringe of neck and shoulders near the center of the back)
Rhomboid.et: From Latin rhomboīdēus as applied in translingual Musculus rhomboideus major and Musculus rhomboideus major and so on.

s: Rheinstetten (a town in western Baden-Württemberg, Germany)
a town in Ostwestfalen-Lippe, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
Rheda-Wiedenbrück.et: From the constituent towns of Rheda and Wiedenbrück (which were united in 1970, but apart from administration still function largely as two neighbouring towns).

s: rheotan (alloy of copper, nickel and zinc used for electrical resistors and heating coils)

... Geitner in Aue in Sachsen und Isabellenhütte in Bonn befassen sich speziell mit der Herstellung solcher Drahtmaterialien. Der Widerstand von Rheotan und Nickelin ist ungefähr 30mal so groß wie der des Kupfers.

Geitner in Aue in Sachsen and Isabellenhütte in Bonn are specifically concerned with the production of such wire materials. The resistance of rheotan and nickelin is approximately 30 times greater than that of copper.
Rheotan - ebenfalls eine Kupfer-Nickel-Legierung - außerordentlich viel gebräuchliches Widerstandsmaterial.
Rheotan - also a copper-nickel alloy - is an extremely common resistance material.
Rheotan.et: Derived from Ancient Greek ῥέω (rhéō, “to flow”).

s: a native or inhabitant of the Rhineland
a rural district of North Rhine-Westphalia; seat: Bergheim
Rhein-Erft-Kreis.et: From the rivers Rhine and Erft.

s: a rural district of Hesse; seat: Bad Schwalbach
Rheingau-Taunus-Kreis.et: From the Rheingau region and the Taunus mountain range.

s: a rural district of Rhineland-Palatinate; seat: Simmern
Rhein-Hunsrück-Kreis.et: From the river Rhine and the Hunsrück mountain range.

s: a rural district of North Rhine-Westphalia; seat: Bergisch Gladbach
Rheinisch-Bergischer Kreis.et: Literally, “district of the Rhine and the Bergisches Land”

s: a rural district of North Rhine-Westphalia; seat: Neuss
a rural district of Rhineland-Palatinate; seat: Bad Ems
Rhein-Lahn-Kreis.et: From the rivers Rhine and Lahn.

s: a rural district of Baden-Württemberg; seat: Heidelberg
Rhein-Neckar-Kreis.et: From the rivers Rhine and Neckar.

s: a rural district of Rhineland-Palatinate; seat: Ludwigshafen
Rhein-Pfalz-Kreis.et: From the names of the river Rhine and the Palatinate region.

s: a rural district of North Rhine-Westphalia; seat: Siegburg
Rhein-Sieg-Kreis.et: From the rivers Rhine and Sieg.

s: a rural district of the Lower Franconia region, Bavaria; seat: Bad Neustadt
Rhön-Grabfeld.et: From the Rhön mountain range and the region of Grabfeld.

s: Low Franconian dialects in the area between Maas, Rhine and Romance languages, with borders to Brabantian (in the West and North-West), Westphalian (in the North-East and East), Ripuarian (in the South-West) and Romance (South-West). Chiefly in reference to the Low Franconian written language of tha
Rheinmaasländisch.et: Rhein + Maas + Land + -isch; coined by Arend Mihm in 1992.

s: in, of or relating to Rheinmaasländisch
A former town, now a quarter of Mönchengladbach, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.
Rheydt.et: From Old Dutch Reithe, of uncertain origin. Possibly a variant of rēda (also attested with th and dh and underlying in several placenames), from Proto-West Germanic *raidu (whence English road). Another possibility would be relation with roden (“to make arable…

s: a right tributary of the Morsbach, Wuppertal district, North Rhine-Westphalia
a right tributary of the Wispe, w:Landkreis Holzminden district, Lower Saxony
a town in Rhein-Sieg-Kreis district, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
a municipal subdivision in Wuppertal, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
A native or resident of Rheinbach
Rheinberg (a town in western North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany)
Rheinberg.et:
First attested as Berka in 1003. The first element Rhein was added by the Dutch in the early 17th century.
Analysable as Rhein (“Rhine”) + Berg (“mountain, hill”).

s: Rheinsberg (a town in northern Brandenburg, Germany)
a bridge that spans the Rhine
Rhine Falls (a waterfall in the Rhine, on the border between canton of Schaffhausen and canton of Zurich, in northern Switzerland)
A village and municipality in Lower Rhine, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.
a native or inhabitant of Rheinberg
rheme (part of a sentence that provides new information regarding the current theme)

There's a profusion of rhododendron in her garden, blooming in a variety of colours.

The Rhine runs between France and Germany.
Cäsar baute eine Brücke über den Rhein.
Caesar built a bridge across the Rhine.
Sie machen eine Bootsfahrt auf dem Rhein.
They are taking a boat trip on the Rhine.

A lot of water has flowed under the bridge since then.
l: Der Rhein ist ein wichtiger Transportweg für Getreide, Kohle, Benzin und Heizöl.
Die Aussicht vom Hoteldach ins Rheintal lockt viele Neugierige ins Papa Rhein.
Eine Gefahr für in und auf dem Rhein lebende Tiere bestehe nicht.

Rhodium is the rarest metal.

Tonight we're having lettuce with rhubarb.

I prefer rhubarb pie to apricot pie.

Tom grows rhubarb.

Rhubarb is a vegetable.

Doch roh sollte man Rhabarber lieber nicht essen.

The music had a pulsating rhythm.
